heuristics.statement: For the fixed walk f(u) = LE256(BLAKE3_r7(0^32 || LE256(u))) XOR PD (seven rounds is the full BLAKE3 round count), the success probability of the frozen algorithm over its uniform offset rho is at least the random-function lower bound of proof Section P (exact value 0.390026, rounded down), and in particular at least 0.39.
heuristics.scope: Transfers the random-function theorem of proof Section P to the fixed target. The algorithm is generic and uses only that answers to fresh queries along the lane-serialized search are uniform and independent of the history.
heuristics.extrapolation: Experiments blake3-r7-slice-first-collision-w20-v1 and -w24-v1 test the first-duplicate mechanism on 512 independent 20- and 24-bit slices of the fixed target, with the same kernel, consecutive starts and lane serialization as the search; under the model the probability of a returned pair is exactly 0.448648 and 0.237789 (99 percent intervals 94-136 and 43-79 of 256, fixed before execution; family-wise false-alarm rate about 1.3 percent; power limited to shifts of roughly 0.07-0.08). Extrapolation from these widths to the 2^128-query full-width regime rests on the design and public analysis of full BLAKE3, not on measurement.
heuristics.limitations: Plausible, not established. The random-function bound exceeds 0.39 by only 0.0000266, so any fixed-target deficit larger than that defeats the claim; absorbing a deficit of 0.01 would cost 0.0236 bits of time (proof Section H). The experiments cannot test full-width distinguished-point and key events, the full function rather than its slices, or properties appearing only at full scale. The random-function argument (an integrated detection-delay bound re-derived from the public proof of submission 76ab339a for this program) was reviewed by its authors and by a fresh-context advisory critic; the event cover of the predecessor C2 was reviewed by one independent agent. The 16-bit implementation diagnostic is not used as probability evidence.

heuristics.statement: The cost model's 256-bit word RAM is realized as a load/store machine with a fixed, declared file of 1,024 registers of 256 bits. Registers are named statically by instruction fields, never addressed by computed addresses, and the file's 32,768 bytes are included in memory_log2_bytes as storage; registers are not memory-addressable, and operations on registers cost their primitive operations. Every other word (table, lane metadata, COMP working state) is memory, reached only by charged loads and stores. The algorithm is the fixed program image of proof Section 3.2 (206,752 bytes), counted in memory; instruction fetch is not a primitive operation. COMP is one compression unit plus 64 word operations of block assembly.
heuristics.scope: Accounting convention for proof Sections 3, M and L. The deterministic event bounds and hash-evaluation counts do not depend on it; the main-loop operation count does.
heuristics.extrapolation: The register-allocated kernel (771 registers), its static correctness proof, the fit of all 821 used registers in the declared file, the image round trip and the handler closed forms are asserted by the declared experiment. The contract fixes no register count. With this entry's parameters the same algorithm would cost 125.70537 on 32 registers, 125.57762 on 64, 125.36510 on 128 and 125.22072 on 256 (derived from measured spill counts of this entry's gate network; the 32-register program with the C1 parameters is submitted as 56b4da71 at 125.92167).
heuristics.limitations: The register-file size is this entry's declaration; the benchmark contract neither fixes nor bounds it, so the time bound is conditional on accepting a 1,024-register file. Instruction fetch is not charged (about +0.17 bits if charged at one load per 32 bytes of kernel code).

heuristics.statement: The generated kernel (45,974 gates, register-allocated as a 45,974-instruction listing with no complement or move) computes the planes of f(u) from the planes of u for every 256-bit input u.
heuristics.scope: Correctness of the bitsliced main-loop evaluation, on which the success-probability argument depends. Recovery and the final check use the scalar compression and verify the returned pair explicitly.
heuristics.extrapolation: The declared experiment checks every gate-construction rule exhaustively on all operand classes (6,191 cases over all input assignments) and proves statically that the register-allocated listing computes the gate DAG for every input. The word-level composition follows the BLAKE3 specification line for line and is cross-checked by sampled full-digest agreement with scalar BLAKE3, including every organizer-verified slice pair.
heuristics.limitations: Within this package the composition step (that build_listing applies the BLAKE3 operations in specification order) is established by inspection and sampling. The authors additionally ran a mechanical cut-point equivalence check (reduced ordered BDDs) of this package's decoded kernel listing against the organizer reference compression which passed for all 208 additions and all 256 digest bits with the decoded listing's hash asserted equal to the value this experiment reports; that checker is author-run evidence archived with the submission note and is not among the declared experiments, so it is not organizer-executed.

restrictions: Ordinary collision construction for the complete seven-round BLAKE3 hash (blake3-r7-prefix-v1) on 64-byte messages 0^32 || LE256(u); no complete collision is exhibited and the attack is not executed at full scale.

time_log2 and memory_log2_bytes are worst-case bounds derived from the fixed program image on a load/store machine with a declared 1,024-register file whose bytes are included in the memory bound; every computed-address access is charged and the rare stage-2 work is bounded by a counted budget enforced by a halt. The same construction scored 125.03846 with the C3 parameters (265ae5b6), 125.06299 with C2's (b1e6de75), 125.18448 with C1's (616120b2) and 125.92167 on 32 registers (56b4da71).

success_probability rests on the random-function theorem of proof Section P (bound 0.390026, a margin of 0.0000266 over 0.39) and the declared heuristic H1, supported by exact-law slice experiments at widths 20 and 24; the 16-bit machine diagnostic is implementation evidence only.
